tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

start_coordinate.description: (x, y): The starting coordinates for `left_click_drag`.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. content.content:
## 5. Account endpoint and balance display

### 5.1 `GET /ent/jusprin/v2/account`

New Django view (plain request handling, on `tsdweb-prod`, next to `/models`), bearer-authenticated like `/models`:

```json
{
  "credits": {"total": 562, "lots": [  // no free lot in the first month
      {"kind": "signup", "credits": 62, "granted": 500, "expires_at": "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z"},
      {"kind": "pack", "credits": 500, "granted": 500, "expires_at": null}]},
  "plan": {"id": "jusprin-workshop-monthly", "name": "Workshop", "renews_at": "...", "unlimited_basic": true,
           "obico_discount": true,
           "auto_reload": false},
  "prices": {"credit_cents": 2, "pack": {"credits": 500, "cents": 1000},
             "plans": [{"id": "jusprin-hobby-monthly", "name": "Hobby", "cents": 1000, "credits": 750},
                       {"id": "jusprin-workshop-monthly", "name": "Workshop", "cents": 2000, "credits": 1000, "unlimited_basic": true}]},
  "usage_30d": {"basic_turns": 140, "expert_turns": 60, "credits": 440,
                "days": [{"date": "2026-11-19", "credits": 60}, ...],
                "activity": [{"date": "2026-11-19", "chat": "Resizing a Print to Fit the Bambu A1 mini", "tier": "expert", "messages": 12, "credits": 60}]},
  "suggestion": {"plan": "jusprin-hobby-monthly", "saves_cents_per_month": 380}
}
```

`days` and `activity` feed the Account page's usage chart and table (boards 4b, 4c: a total for 30 days, a bar per day, a row per chat with tier, messages and credits, plus reward rows). The composer's hover panel needs only `credits` and `plan`.

`/jusprin/api/me/` stays as the sign-in check; the app calls `/account` after a sign-in check, after every completed or failed turn on the `jusprin` provider (one small GET, no streaming change), when the Preferences account section opens, and when the window regains focus after the person was sent to the browser to buy. A cheaper later step is a `X-JusPrin-Credits` response header on the stream start, but `AgentTransport` does not surface response headers today, so the GET comes first.

### 5.2 In the app

Synced to canvas version 79 (Kenneth's review, 2026-11-02). The boards are the source of truth for wording; `pricing-touchpoints-design-2026-11.md` lists them per point.

- **A chat keeps its model** (Kenneth, 2026-11-02, "for now"): the tier is chosen before the person's first message in a chat and never changes after. A turn the app started (the file-opened report) does not count: it runs on Expert and leaves the pickers live (3.3). Once a chat has a message from the person, the model and thinking pickers stay in the composer, greyed, and hovering shows a two-line tooltip: "A chat keeps the model and thinking level it started with. Start a new chat to change them." / "Each message you send in this chat costs 5 credits." (board 2c). `Composer.tsx` today disables the pickers only while the Agent responds; that becomes "disabled once the chat has a message". `chat-history-cache-plan.md` D5 (a switch within one wire format) is superseded for now.
- **Model picker** (`ModelPickers.tsx`): each option shows its price from `ModelOptionInfo.credits` with its unit, "Expert · 5 credits a message" and "Standard · 1 credit a message" (never "1 credit" alone), plus one clause on when to use it. On Workshop the Standard option reads "Standard · 0 credits a message". Only Expert has a thinking picker. BYOK options show no price. The option stays this short; Kenneth rejected a clause about pictures (2026-11-02).
- **A picture in a Standard chat** (decided 2026-11-02, board 3e): the staged attachment row (`AttachmentChip.tsx`: thumbnail, name, second line, Remove) carries the notice. In a chat whose model has `images: false`, a staged picture keeps its thumbnail, its second line reads "Standard can't see pictures, so this one will not be sent.", styled as the design system's warning (triangle-alert glyph in status-warning beside primary ink), and Remove is the only action on the row (Kenneth: "remove 'new expert chat' button"). Send stays enabled; the gateway drops the image blocks and leaves its text note (3.4). The host also leaves the picture-returning tools (`view_render` and the others that return images) out of a Standard chat's tool list, keyed on the model's `images` flag from `GET /models`.
- **Balance** (a new `account` host message with the JSON above): the composer shows only a small ring of what is left, no number, no animation (board 2a, "just like how claude code behaves"). Hover or tap opens the panel: "562 credits left." (credits only, Kenneth 2026-11-02; no message count), then a bar per lot, grouped only by expiry, soonest first, labelled by kind with what is left and its date ("First-month credits · 62 of 500 left · Expires 1 Dec"; "Free credits · 50 of 50 left · Expires 2 Dec"; "Bought credits · 500 of 500 left · Never expire"; on Workshop "Workshop credits · 640 of 1,000 left · Expires 1 Dec. Unused credits don't carry over."), fill = what is left; "Expiring credits are used first."; actions "Get more credits" and "See usage". Free credits get the same ring as any others (Kenneth, board 6a), with no line about them in the composer. The bars need each lot's original size, so `lots[]` carries `granted`; a `reward` lot never expires but is not bought, so the panel needs a label for it (no board shows one yet, decision 13); what the ring measures against is open (the board uses the sum of every lot's `granted`, a placeholder). No ring on BYOK.
- **Before sending** (board 3b): the app knows the balance and the chat's tier, so when the next message cannot be paid, Send is disabled and one line says why: "You have 3 credits; this Expert chat needs 5 a message." The one action is "Get more credits", which opens the pricing page. There is no "New Standard chat", no "Send with Standard" and no "Switch this chat to Standard". Earlier than that (board 3a), once, the composer says "About 25 credits left" with "Get more credits".
- **Exhaustion** (board 3c, reached only by a race between two sends): the 402 drives the failed-message card with the same words, "This message needs 5 credits; you have 3.", the same single action, and the message returned to the composer. `ProviderAgent::http_error` passes the gateway's message through instead of its fixed text when the code is `credits_exhausted`.
- **"Get more credits" everywhere** (Kenneth, board 3c): outside the pricing page there is no "Buy" beside "Subscribe", because nobody can judge a pack against a plan from a button label. The savings alert (5.3) keeps "Subscribe" because it names one plan and shows the sums.
- **Preferences › Account** (boards 4a to 4c): the signed-in email and sign out; the plan line ("Workshop · $16 a month. Renews 1 Dec. Obico Premium Subscriber: 20% off subscriptions.") with "Manage plan" and "Get more credits"; the same balance panel as the composer; Usage (30-day total, bars per day, the table from `activity`, "See all activity"); the alert switch, whose sub-line is "Once, above the message box." Where this page renders is section 5.4.
- **BYOK unchanged:** none of this appears for providers with an API key.
- **Design:** every colour, size and radius through the token file and `ShellTheme` or CSS variables per `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`. The boards exist (canvas version 79, captures in `design-captures/credits-2026-11/`); the tooltip on 2c needs two lines where the design system's tooltip has one, so that is a token change first.

### 5.3 The "subscription would save you money" alert (decided)

Computed server-side in `/account` from the last 30 days of `CreditCharge`:

- cost at the Pay as you go price = credits × 2¢;
- cost on Hobby = $10 + max(0, credits − 750) × 2¢;
- cost on Workshop = $20 + max(0, expert credits − 1,000) × 2¢ (basic turns cost 0);
- apply the 20% Obico discount when it applies;
- `suggestion` names the cheapest plan when it saves at least $3 a month against what the person is doing now (pack, or current plan). It never names Pay as you go: the reverse alert, telling a subscriber that Pay as you go would cost less, was removed with board 7c.

The app shows it once as a dismissable line above the composer and in Preferences › Account, re-evaluated when the 30-day window changes the answer. Preferences › Account has the switch "Alert me when a subscription would save me money", on by default (the message is in the person's favour; the switch exists so it can be silenced). The caveat from the brainstorm stands: this recruits exactly the heavy users, which is why the plans give 1.5× and not 2× the pack rate.

### 5.4 Where the Account and pricing pages render (recommend: the server)

**Not decided. Do not build either way until Kenneth chooses (decision 12 in section 12).** What follows is a recommendation with its reasons, not the plan.

Kenneth asked (2026-11-02) whether the server should serve the account and pricing pages into a webview instead of the app building them from the `/account` API. His reasons: pricing will be experimented with a lot, so changing it must not need an app release, and old app versions must not keep showing stale prices. I agree, and recommend this split:

- **Composer: API.** The ring, the hover panel, the picker prices and the pre-send check render inside the composer on every keystroke and must degrade when offline, so they stay on `/account` and `/models`. That API returns numbers and names only, which keeps it cheap to hold backward compatible.
- **Account and pricing: server pages in a webview.** Boards 4a to 4c and 5a, 5b become one web page under `web_ent/jusprin/v2/` (templates or the existing Vue app, rendered with the person's data), opened in a second `AgentWebView` from Preferences › Account and from every "Get more credits". The desktop implementation of those boards moves from the client repo to tsd-enterprise. Steam does exactly this for its store and account pages inside the native client.
- **Signing the webview in:** the app holds an OAuth bearer token; the page needs a session. Never put the token in the URL (it ends up in logs). New endpoint `POST /ent/jusprin/v2/webview_session` (bearer): returns a single-use URL valid for 60 seconds; the webview opens it, the view logs the session in with Django's `login()` and redirects to the page. This endpoint is the real new cost, about a day with tests (single use, expiry, wrong user).
- **Theme and tokens:** the app passes `?theme=light|dark` and the page uses the same token CSS as the Agent page (`bundle.css` variables), so it is not a second design system.
- **Checkout stays in the system browser:** the served pricing page hands off to Chargebee's hosted page in the default browser, as section 4 already says; my expectation, not verified, is that 3-D Secure redirects are what breaks inside embedded webviews. The app refreshes `/account` on window focus.
- **Bridge contract:** two messages from the page to the app, `credits_changed` and `close`, and nothing else, so a three-year-old app still works with today's page. The page never calls back into the host for data.
- **Offline:** the page shows a plain "can't reach JusPrin" state with a retry, not a browser error; the composer keeps the last `/account` answer.
- **Latency:** a remote page takes a visible moment to appear in Preferences › Account; acceptable there, which is one more reason the composer stays on the API.

## 6. Workshop's Standard messages
## 12. Decisions still Kenneth's

On 2026-11-02 evening, after seeing canvas version 73, Kenneth corrected the credits design in four ways:

- Every credit is the same. No Standard-only ("basic_only", "trickle") lot. Free accounts (not subscribed) get 50 credits a month, expiring one month after grant, that pay for either tier. Not "everyone": he told the design session "the 'everyone gets 50 credits' wording is wrong. I never said that." I had told the design session "yes, everyone" as my own pick before he answered; never pass my pick on as his. His words: "let's just give free users 50/mo use-it-or-loose it credits".
- Workshop has no ceiling. "no ceiling. It's probably easier just to say standard messages cost 0 credits". Nothing about 600 or fair use remains.
- A balance is one number of credits, never "N Standard or N Expert messages" beside it ("showing a number of messages and credits at the same time is fucking confusing"). The translation line was my addition in the design doc, never his decision. Bars are grouped only by expiry; bought credits get a bar too (decision 13 closed).
- "New Standard chat" and board 3d are gone, since the case only existed because of the Standard-only lot.

Prices in messages appear only where the person chooses or is stopped: picker options, the stop card for the chat's tier, the pricing page's one sentence, the low-balance notice, and one scale line under the first-month offer.

**Why:** he said he was "seriously worried that we are not on the same page" and asked me to restate the plan; the Standard-only lot and the ceiling were placeholders the plan carried without his words behind them.

**How to apply:** before presenting any credits surface, check it against these four. When a plan carries a mechanism (a lot kind, a cap) with no quote from Kenneth behind it, flag it as mine rather than drawing it on every board. Related: [[credit-price-needs-its-unit]], [[usage-against-quota-common-shape]], [[trace-a-rule-to-kenneths-words]].

Later the same evening Kenneth reviewed every mechanism that was mine, not his. Kept: the launch offer, "About 25 credits left" (credits, not messages), "Expiring credits are used first", the savings switch on by default, the Account page shape, Standard as the default tier after the first month, the v1 welcome-back fill-ins, the print-report form details, the alias ids. Dropped: the reverse savings alert and board 7c, the month-end and 7-day expiry notices, the daily cap on free app turns, the thinking picker on Standard. Expiry: every expiring lot expires one month from the day it was granted, never at a calendar month end. His message was only a keep list, so anything left off it counts as dropped. A session wrongly called the report rules "neither kept nor dropped"; he corrected that the same day: "I thought the clawback are removed, rigth? And why is it still a placeholder?" The clawback is removed. Asked about 25 credits, three a day and stopping after two invalid reports, he ruled: "Remove these. only keep the 1st one". A report earns 25 credits, one per G-code, and a review is only recorded.

Ruled later: "no 50 credits for first month. only 500 initial credits. pack holders also get 50 credits a month." The 50 a month goes to every account not on a subscription, starting after the first month; the balance example is 62 + 500 = 562 with no Free credits bar.

Your own API key · one row per provider

Decided 2026-10-21; replaces the provider tabs. Every provider has its own row, so you can see at a glance which ones have a key. Agent setup and Preferences › Agent use the same row (Design System › Agent/Provider Row). The app keeps each provider’s key on this computer and can show its start and last 4 characters; it records no dates, so none are shown. Key characters are examples.
1. No key
Only Add key. Nothing looks filled in.
2. Entering a key
Placeholder text only, no bullets: an empty field never looks filled in. Paste sits in the field; Check key waits for a key.
3. Checking
The key being checked stays visible and locked, so it is clear which one is in question. Cancel stops the check.
4. Couldn’t check
The provider couldn’t be reached. Nothing was saved, so this isn’t a rejection.
5. Key saved
A saved key is read-only: its start and last 4 characters at full contrast. It never shows as bullets.
6. Replacing
Replace opens an empty field for the new key. The saved key stays until the new one passes its check; Cancel keeps it.
7. Rejected
The provider refused the saved key. Its last 4 characters stay visible so the person knows which key failed.
8. Working until restart
The key passed but couldn’t be stored on this computer. It works now and will be asked for again after a restart.

commit 641c17f13e46a2deefccf1d886eec9e7091f0ed5
Author: Kenneth Jiang <k@obico.io>
Date:   Fri Oct 23 02:05:19 2026 +0000

    Add JusPrin's own Preferences window
    
    JusPrin's Preferences replaces OrcaSlicer's dialog for everyday use. It is
    one window that opens over any screen, from the gear on Home and from
    Preferences... in a project's menu. It is a
    React page (PreferencesApp) driven by PreferencesWindow, with every setting
    read and written through PreferencesSettings on the same AppConfig keys
    OrcaSlicer uses, so the classic view and JusPrin agree.
    
    Sections: Account, Agent (the shared Agent connection rows), Appearance,
    3D view, Projects & files and Updates. Nothing about Bambu Cloud and no
    expert options; "OrcaSlicer preferences..." opens OrcaSlicer's dialog
    unchanged. Dark mode calls the same OrcaSlicer functions the dialog's
    checkbox does. The language list is built from the installed
    translations; a new language is saved at once and takes effect when
    JusPrin restarts ("Restart now" or "Later"), because rebuilding the window
    in place left the old Edge process on the old language and every web page
    then failed to load. Restart now saves the project and starts a fresh
    JusPrin with the same command line; if the save is refused, JusPrin stays
    open and says why. The design is the "Preferences" page on the JusPrin v2
    canvas (2026-10-21).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

I couldn't find any later answer from you on that decision, in memory or in code.

So I looked for everything else that was held back with step 3, and then compared every Preferences board with the code.

**Missing because they were held back with billing:**

1. **The plan price and a "Manage plan" button** (board 4c, "Workshop · $16 a month"). Billing doesn't exist yet, so there is no plan to manage.
2. **The savings alert.** On boards 7a and 7b, a pay-as-you-go user sees one line above the message box, such as "Hobby would have saved you $5.00 in the last 30 days", with "See the sums" and "Subscribe". Preferences › Account would have the switch "Alert me when a subscription would save me money", on by default. You kept this on 11-02. Neither side is built: the server's account endpoint always returns `suggestion: None`.
3. **The "+500 credits" line** that board 9 shows when you come back from buying. There's no buying yet. Related, and from my own work: the Agent page fetches the account again when its window gets focus, but the Preferences window doesn't. Once buying exists, Account would show the old balance until you reopen it.
4. **"Bought N credits" rows** in the usage table. The server doesn't send them.

**Missing from Preferences, reason unknown:**

5. **Account section:** an "Email and account details" row ("Change your email or delete your account in your browser", with an "Open in browser" button), and the line "Signing out keeps your projects, printers and API keys on this computer." Neither has ever been in the code.
6. **Agent › "New chats start with":** the board has a Thinking row ("Higher levels answer more carefully, and more slowly", default Medium). The code only has Model.

The Preferences window was built on 10-23. My earliest saved copy of that board is from 11-01, so I can't tell whether these rows were added to the board later or skipped when it was built.

**Differences that are deliberate, so not missing:**
- **Language:** the board says the window reloads. The code asks you to restart instead. Commit 641c17f13e4 explains why: reloading in place left the embedded browser on the old language, and every web page then failed to load.
- **The Model row's hint:** the code says "A chat keeps the model it started with." That follows your 11-02 rule. The board's "Any chat can switch from its message box" is out of date.
- **The "This model needs an OpenAI key… Add a key…" notice** on the board about where Preferences opens isn't in the code. I haven't checked whether the model picker can still reach that state, so it may be obsolete.

The other sections match their boards: Appearance (apart from Language), 3D view, Projects & files, Updates in all five states, the sign-in states and the API key rows.

**Decision needed: should the Account and pricing pages stay in the app, or move to web pages our server shows inside the app?** This is your call because it decides which repository the billing screens get built in. The usage section I just built lives in the app, and it reads the account endpoint, so it already leans toward the in-app answer. The plan recommended server pages because you wanted to change prices without shipping an app release, and without old app versions showing stale prices. That costs about a day for a one-time sign-in link into the embedded page, plus moving the usage section I just built over to the server. Keeping everything in the app costs nothing now, but every price change then needs a release. I'd pick server pages for the pricing page, where prices change, and keep Account in the app as it is now. Which way do you want it?

The usage section is still not committed to jusprin-newui.
